Last reviewed: 2026-10-25. Package versions, SDK versions, and negotiated MCP
protocol revisions are separate compatibility boundaries.

## Release lines

| Package release | MCP SDK | MCP protocol | Support and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.15.0 | server/client 2.3.1, Node adapter 2.1.1 (exact pins) | Native `2026-07-28` plus older clients on the same endpoint | Current release, 194 tools across 22 domains, Node.js 24+. HTTP session and replay stores are retired; obsolete settings warn and are ignored. First warnings and ignored settings start in 0.15.0; session/replay behavior is removed in that release. |
| 0.14.1 | v1; dependency floor 1.32.1 | Latest supported revision: `2025-11-25` | Previous line, 194 tools across 22 domains, Node.js 24+. Stateful HTTP sessions and optional replay stores remain active. |
| 0.13.0 | v1; dependency floor 1.31.0 | Latest supported revision: `2025-11-25` | Historical release, 184 tools across 20 domains. Upgrade to the latest minor for security fixes. |

The 0.14.x SDK supports `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`,
`2024-11-05`, and `2024-10-07`. A newer client that negotiates an older
revision can use this server; that fallback does not mean the server natively
supports `2026-07-28`. Release tests cover modern auto/pinned clients and default legacy clients over HTTP and stdio. Client products, deployed proxies and marketplace acceptance still need release validation.

[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/CodesWhat/portkey-admin-mcp/blob/46556acebb77c9ee224e54836137c64fb5650594/SECURITY.md) owns the security-support policy: fixes ship on the
latest published minor line; older minor lines do not receive backports.
See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/CodesWhat/portkey-admin-mcp/blob/46556acebb77c9ee224e54836137c64fb5650594/CHANGELOG.md) for changes in each published release.

## Configuration lifecycle

No deprecation warnings or removals for the settings below shipped in 0.14.x.
As of 0.15.0, the listed settings warn and are ignored, and the underlying
session/replay behavior is removed. There was no intermediate warning-only
release. Obsolete names remain recognized for warnings; this does not retain
their former functionality. 0.14.x is the previous line and is unchanged.

| Setting or behavior | 0.14.x | 0.15.0 behavior | First warning / ignored / removal release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MCP_SESSION_MODE`, `MCP_SESSION_TIMEOUT` | Active; stateful mode is the default | Ignored with a warning; older clients use stateless requests | 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 |
| `MCP_EVENT_STORE`, `MCP_EVENT_TTL_SECONDS`, `MCP_EVENT_STORE_MAX_EVENTS`, `MCP_EVENT_STORE_MAX_BYTES`, `MCP_EVENT_STORE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` | Active replay configuration | Ignored with a warning; authenticated GET/DELETE return 405 (auth and Origin checks still apply first: 401 without credentials, 403 for a disallowed Origin) | 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 |
| `MCP_EVENT_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `MCP_REDIS_KEY_PREFIX` | Active Redis replay configuration | Ignored with a warning | 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 |
| HTTP GET stream, `Last-Event-ID` recovery, session identifiers | Active under the configured HTTP mode | No session IDs are returned; authenticated GET/DELETE, including legacy session or `Last-Event-ID` headers, return 405. Unauthenticated requests get 401 and a disallowed Origin gets 403 | 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 / 0.15.0 |
| `RATE_LIMIT_*` | Active rate-limit configuration | Retained, including shared Redis limiting | No removal planned |
| `RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL`, `MCP_REDIS_URL`, `REDIS_URL` | Rate limiter uses these URL sources in that order; replay uses the latter two | Documented Redis connection path for rate limiting is preserved now that replay is retired | No removal assigned |
| `MCP_MAX_SESSIONS` | Bounds stateful sessions or active stateless request handlers | Retain the stateless concurrency bound | No removal planned |
| `MCP_TOOL_DOMAINS`, `CORS_ORIGIN` | Supported fallbacks for `PORTKEY_TOOL_DOMAINS`, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | No change assigned | No removal planned |

Redis rate limiting and Redis replay are separate features. Retiring the replay
store does not remove the need for a shared rate limiter in multi-instance or
serverless deployments. Keep working settings on a 0.14.x deployment until you
upgrade to 0.15.0.

## Migration notes

The migration shipped in 0.15.0, ahead of the original 2026-12-01 start-by
date and the 2027-01-27 completion target. Those were project planning dates,
not announced configuration-removal dates or an SDK end-of-life guarantee.
[ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/CodesWhat/portkey-admin-mcp/blob/46556acebb77c9ee224e54836137c64fb5650594/ROADMAP.md) tracks follow-up work.

Operators upgrading from 0.14.x need an upgrade guide covering:

- warning and removal behavior for every retired setting;
- loss of session affinity, the GET stream, and `Last-Event-ID` recovery;
- how to inspect Portkey state after an interrupted mutation before retrying,
  since an automatic retry can repeat a successful write;
- retained Redis rate-limit configuration and concurrency bounds; and
- client, reverse-proxy, Vercel, and marketplace compatibility checks.

The release updated this table, the README configuration reference,
[architecture](/docs/architecture/), [Vercel guide](/docs/http-deployment/),
[security assurance case](/docs/security/), and changelog together.

## Interrupted requests

The SDK v2 server keeps older `initialize` clients working on `/mcp` without
persistent HTTP sessions. Modern clients use `server/discover` on the same URL.
Clients and proxies must forward `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method` and, for
named operations such as `tools/call`, `Mcp-Name`. Tool filters apply to every
request; reuse the same `?tools=` URL throughout a client workflow.

GET streams, DELETE session operations and `Last-Event-ID` replay are retired.
A disconnected request can still have changed Portkey state even when its result
was lost. Do not automatically replay a write:

1. Save the operation name, target workspace/resource ID and intended change
   without recording credentials or secret values.
2. Reconnect and use the matching `get_*` or `list_*` tool, or the Portkey
   dashboard, to inspect whether the change completed. For creates, correlate
   the intended name/metadata and time; a missing response is not proof of failure.
3. If the desired state already exists, continue from that resource. If failure
   is confirmed, retry once intentionally. If the outcome is still ambiguous,
   inspect the upstream audit/usage records or ask the tenant administrator before
   repeating creates, completions or other operations with side effects.

Reads can be requested again. Neither transport reconnect nor a successful new
handshake proves a previous mutation failed. There is no exactly-once guarantee.
`MCP_MAX_SESSIONS` now caps concurrent request handlers; it does not restore
sessions or replay. Redis remains available for shared rate limiting through
`RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL`, `MCP_REDIS_URL`, then `REDIS_URL`. No replay encryption key
is needed. Keep deployed 0.14.x settings until upgrading; the first
warning, ignored-setting and feature-removal release is 0.15.0.
